source.title: A random matrix theory approach to damping in deep learning
source.authors: Diego Granziol; Samuel Albanie; Xingchen Wan; Stephen J. Roberts

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present, with some extraction and OCR formatting artifacts in equations and tables.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies damping and learning-rate settings for adaptive optimizers, then measures held-out performance and training behavior. This bears conceptually on V4, but does not reproduce the original optimizer comparisons or tuning protocol.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results for damping changes and optimizer comparisons. Cited results from other work are not extracted. Figures 4–15 are not used to infer precise values where the text does not state them.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out image-classification performance and tests whether tuning damping removes their performance gap. It is not an original source for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conjecture that noisy estimates of flat directions contribute to the adaptive generalization gap, show that damping tuning can remove it in selected image-classification experiments, and propose a Hessian-variance-based damping learner. Learned damping alone gives Adam only small improvements; an alternative learning-rate schedule is needed to surpass SGD in that experiment. The causal explanation remains a conjecture, and the learner requires expensive Hessian estimates.
record.recipe_differences: Tests damping and online Hessian-variance-based damping in SGD, Adam, AdamW, and KFAC experiments; it does not reproduce the cited optimizer-comparison protocols.
record.method_sensitivity: Damping, global learning rate, optimizer, batch normalization, decoupled weight decay, and learning-rate schedule change the reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: KFAC damping changes affect validation accuracy despite similar training performance; larger damping also improves Adam validation performance with batch normalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Damping influences held-out performance within an adaptive optimizer, independently of establishing an advantage or disadvantage relative to SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned damping improves KFAC convergence speed and stability relative to fixed damping.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hessian-variance-based damping can accelerate and stabilize KFAC training.

fits_no_version.finding: Restricting movement in sharp directions worsens logistic-regression generalization more than training performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative movement along sharp and flat directions affects generalization in the tested convex classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing damping reduces Hessian spectral norm without consistently improving generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unnormalized Hessian spectral norm does not reliably rank held-out performance across these damping settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam and KFAC permit higher selected stable learning rates than SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice changes the maximum stable global learning rate in this VGG-16 setup.

record.problems: Experiments are restricted mainly to computer-vision datasets and a small set of architectures. The paper itself says its results are limited in scope; several comparisons are presented in figures without exact values in prose, and vanilla Adam on ImageNet is a single-seed result.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible result rows were omitted. Table 1 contains flattened spectral-norm and validation-accuracy entries that cannot be reliably assigned to individual configurations from the supplied layout; those entries are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width required to fit training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and learned local connectivity.

Language benchmarks, word-level language models, switching from Adam to SGD, and a systematic comparison of decoupled versus coupled weight decay. The study does not reproduce Wilson et al.'s tuning protocol or establish prevalence across benchmarks.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects and its removal together with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and retraining against random-removal controls.

missing.what: Figure 2's own optimizer comparison: VGG-16 validation accuracy is 94.3 for SGD and 95.1 for Adam at epoch 300. The caption identifies CIFAR-10, while nearby prose inconsistently says CIFAR-100; preserve this ambiguity.

Record the training-performance comparison accompanying the default-damping held-out gap: Figure 1 and Section 3.2 report SGD outperforming Adam without weight decay or batch normalization, using their respective best settings, despite both fitting training data closely.

record.verdict_notes: Only V4 is tested. Recovery after broader tuning qualifies the limited-tuning disadvantage and agrees with V4's explicit qualification; it does not challenge the full version. Paired comparator rows are not independent evidence. No exact figure-only values or statistical significance beyond the reported comparisons are inferred.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.

Does not test the limited-tuning comparison across image and language benchmarks, broader tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, or word-level language models. Tests damping changes in Adam and KFAC, including comparisons with SGD.
Large-batch effects and adaptation of training recipes.
Dropout and its interaction with data augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized training examples and retraining.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.note: SGD comparator in the same table: 65.3 ± 0.6. The paper says Adam-D closes the gap and can match or beat SGD.
rows.check: Relative to SGD's 65.3 ± 0.6 accuracy, tuned Adam's 65.5 ± 0.7 shows the adaptive disadvantage removed; it does not establish a reliable advantage. Increasing damping is a training hyperparameter change, not a post-training weight edit.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.note: Reference result for comparison with Adam and Adam-D.
rows.check: Use the paired default-Adam result, 61.9 ± 0.4, as the comparator: SGD reaches 65.3 ± 0.6. This reference row is not an independent replication of R3.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.note: The table marks the vanilla Adam ImageNet value as a single-seed result, but does not mark the CIFAR-100 value as a single-seed result; values are reproduced as printed.
rows.check: The CIFAR-100 result uses five seeds, not one. Against SGD's 65.3 ± 0.6, default Adam reaches 61.9 ± 0.4.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Increased AdamW numerical stability constant to δ = 1e−4

conditions.value: 3 for Adam-D and SGD; single seed for Adam

rows.note: The authors say increased δ can match and surpass SGD. Table 2 gives SGD as 75.7 ± 0.1 and marks vanilla Adam with an asterisk because it was not run for multiple seeds.
rows.check: Tuned AdamW reaches 76.6 ± 0.1 versus SGD's 75.7 ± 0.1, reversing the adaptive disadvantage. Table 2 abbreviates the optimizer as Adam, but the experimental text specifies AdamW. This is a training hyperparameter change.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.note: Reference result for comparison with Adam and Adam-D.
rows.check: Against default AdamW's single-seed 74.04, SGD reaches 75.7 ± 0.1. This is a paired reference, not independent evidence beyond R6.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.note: The asterisk says this is a single-seed result reported for completeness.
rows.check: Add SGD's 75.7 ± 0.1 as comparator. Default AdamW reaches 74.04; its single-seed status limits precision.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Increased Adam damping; text reports δ = 0.005 and 0.0075 settings match or beat the SGD baseline

conditions.value: α = 0.0004 for the largest rate at which Adam trains with default damping
no weight decay or batch normalization

rows.value: Adam with larger damping can match or beat SGD on validation while converging faster
rows.note: Textual result; no exact accuracy for these settings is stated in the prose.
rows.check: The matching or better settings use learning rate 0.001 and damping 0.005 or 0.0075. Learning rate 0.0004 describes the largest stable default-damping baseline. Separate these conditions; the text establishes removal of the disadvantage but does not assign exact outcomes to each tuned setting.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Increased KFAC damping while varying learning rate

conditions.value: no weight decay or batch normalization

rows.baseline: KFAC settings with lower damping, as listed in Table 1
rows.value: As Rest-curv increases, validation accuracy worsens; at α = 0.0001, reducing δ from 0.0003 to 0.0001 lowers validation accuracy from 60.2% to 56%
rows.note: The passage reports a direction of effect and two accuracy values, but also says training performance is effectively unchanged and the generalization drop is larger than the training-accuracy drop.
rows.check: This compares KFAC configurations without an SGD comparator, so it cannot establish V4's optimizer disadvantage or its removal. The baseline description also reverses the damping direction: decreasing damping from 0.0003 to 0.0001 lowers accuracy from 60.2% to 56%.

rows.subject: VGG-16BN
rows.operation_detail: Increased Adam damping with batch normalization and decoupled weight decay
rows.value: Larger damping slightly assists training and improves generalization, with and without weight decay
rows.note: The authors characterize the improvements as slight; figure does not provide a textual exact value.
rows.check: Improvement between Adam configurations with and without weight decay does not establish their performance relative to SGD. No quantitative or explicit SGD comparison is supplied for this experiment.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: KFAC with damping learned from Hessian variance, updated every 100 training iterations
rows.baseline: Fixed damping values, including low values that diverge and higher values that converge slowly
rows.value: Learned damping is relatively insensitive to the initial value; all three initial values converge significantly faster than fixed-damping methods
rows.note: This result is about optimization speed and stability; the passage does not state a test accuracy for these settings.
rows.check: This is the proposed damping learner's optimization speed and stability result, without held-out performance. It should not be a V4 evidence row.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: KFAC with damping learned from Hessian variance, updated every 100 training iterations
rows.baseline: Fixed damping δ = 0.1 and the SGD test result on three times as many training epochs
rows.value: The learned damping initialized at 0.03 beats the generalization performance of fixed δ = 0.1 and the cited SGD result
rows.note: The prose states the comparison but does not give exact accuracy values.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports learned-damping KFAC exceeding the SGD held-out result. Specify that KFAC trains for 100 epochs while the SGD reference trains for 300; this is not an equal-budget comparison. The SGD reference is the study's own baseline.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: KFAC with damping learned from Hessian variance, updated every 100 training iterations
rows.value: Learned damping reaches a comparable generalization score faster
rows.note: The authors also report that a fixed initial damping of 0.03 converges somewhat less quickly but trains and generalizes better than the lower starting damping counterpart.
rows.check: This compares learned and fixed damping within KFAC, chiefly for convergence speed, without establishing a comparison with SGD. It is method-performance evidence rather than a V4 result.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Adam with learned damping from Hessian variance, with an alternative learning-rate ramp-up schedule

conditions.value: base rate increased by factor 5 early, then decreased

rows.baseline: Standard Adam damping baseline and SGD
rows.value: Learned damping with the alternative schedule boosts validation performance and surpasses SGD; improvement is described as small and does not make up the gap in the earlier setup
rows.note: The paper says auto-damping alone improves convergence and validation over the standard baseline but does not close the gap with SGD; an alternative schedule is needed to surpass it.
rows.check: Split the conditions. With the ordinary schedule, auto-damped Adam improves slightly but remains worse than SGD; with the alternative ramp-up schedule, it surpasses SGD. The extracted value incorrectly combines these outcomes into one condition.

rows.subject: Logistic regression
rows.operation_detail: Compared training and validation error under LanczosOPT damping and explicit reduction of movement in selected sharp directions
rows.measure: training and validation error change as damping and sharp-direction perturbation vary
rows.value: Increasing Rest-curv worsens generalization; stronger perturbations harm generalization more than training
rows.note: This is a LanczosOPT/GD convex logistic-regression experiment, not one of the claim versions' listed settings.
rows.check: The sharp-direction intervention in logistic regression does not measure any supplied version. Its own reported effect is clear, but 'observed' cannot describe a linked version here.

rows.subject: Logistic regression
rows.operation_detail: Compared training and validation error under LanczosOPT damping and explicit reduction of movement in selected sharp directions
rows.value: The authors report an identical pattern to MNIST at slightly higher testing error
rows.note: This is not one of the claim versions' listed settings.
rows.check: As in R14, this is a sharp-direction intervention rather than a test of a supplied version.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Measured spectral norm λ1 alongside validation accuracy across Adam and KFAC learning-rate/damping settings
rows.value: Increasing damping always leads to smaller spectral norm, but this does not always coincide with better generalization
rows.note: This is not the magnitude-scaled perturbation sharpness measure in V7; Table 1's flattened entries are not assigned to individual settings here.
rows.check: Hessian spectral norm is not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure, and validation accuracy alone is not its specified generalization gap.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Searched for the highest stable learning rate for each optimizer
rows.note: The paper interprets this as evidence that adaptive methods better estimate sharp directions than SGD, and KFAC better than Adam.
rows.check: These are selected maximum stable learning rates, not held-out performance or a supplied version's effect. Exclude this selection result from claim-evidence rows.

relationships.condition: Default damping: VGG-16 on CIFAR-100 and ResNet-50 on ImageNet
relationships.reason: Default Adam/AdamW trails SGD: 61.9 versus 65.3 and 74.04 versus 75.7 accuracy, respectively (R2–R3, R5–R6); ImageNet AdamW uses one seed.
relationships.display_finding: The reported accuracy deficits for default Adam and AdamW relative to SGD remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Adam/AdamW with tuned damping and learning rate
relationships.reason: The disadvantage disappears on CIFAR-100 (65.5 versus SGD's 65.3) and reverses on ImageNet (76.6 versus 75.7), supporting V4's broader-tuning qualification (R1, R4, R7).
relationships.display_finding: Tuned Adam and AdamW reportedly exceeded SGD accuracy, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Auto-damped Adam with the ordinary learning-rate schedule on CIFAR-100
relationships.reason: Section 7.3 explicitly says the small improvements leave Adam below SGD; R13 must separate this condition from ramp-up training.
relationships.display_finding: The reported small improvements from automatic damping, still leaving Adam below SGD, remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Auto-damped Adam with the alternative ramp-up schedule on CIFAR-100
relationships.reason: Section 7.3 explicitly reports performance above SGD after changing the schedule, showing recipe dependence; R13 must be split.
relationships.display_finding: Changing the ramp-up schedule reportedly raised auto-damped Adam above SGD, but this result remains unverified.

relationships.reason: KFAC exceeds the study's SGD held-out result after 100 versus 300 epochs, extending the tuning qualification to a second-order adaptive method (R11).
relationships.display_finding: Learned-damping KFAC reportedly exceeded SGD accuracy with fewer epochs, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: VGG-16 on CIFAR-10, optimizer settings unspecified in Figure 2
relationships.reason: Figure 2 reports Adam validation accuracy of 95.1 versus SGD's 94.3; this text-based verdict has no extracted row and its tuning conditions are unspecified.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly exceeded SGD validation accuracy, but the comparison remains unverified and optimizer tuning was unspecified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: VGG-16 on CIFAR-100 and ResNet50 on ImageNet with increased Adam/AdamW damping
reader_labels.reason: Increased damping improves held-out performance; Adam-D slightly exceeds the SGD reference on CIFAR-100, and Adam-D exceeds SGD on ImageNet (R1, R4, R7).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: KFAC damping sweeps and Adam learned-damping experiments
reader_labels.reason: Damping effects depend on learning rate and schedule: higher curvature learning-rate ratio worsens generalization, and Adam auto-damping without the alternative schedule does not close its gap with SGD (R8, R11, R13).
